PullRequest.Title: chat: surface MCP sign-in above the session input
PullRequest.Body:
Show MCP servers that require authentication in the existing pill row above the Agents Window chat input, instead of leaving sign-in buried in server management.

- Disabled by default behind `chat.agentSessions.mcpAuthPill.enabled` (`experimental`, `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`). Enable via an experiment or set it to `true` for team dogfooding; saved pill preferences cannot bypass the gate. Changes take effect without reload.
- Only enabled servers in the current session with `AuthRequired` appear.
- One server offers **Sign In to {name}** or **Grant Additional Access to {name}** according to the authentication reason; several collapse into a neutral **MCP Servers Need Attention** dropdown.
- Entries disappear when authenticated, disabled, or removed. Cancelled authentication remains actionable.
- Reuses the existing authentication service, pill components, and visibility menu. No new authentication logic or CSS.

## Validation

- Rebased onto latest `microsoft/vscode` main.
- 63 focused tests pass, including session isolation, state transitions, authentication routing, rendered toolbar visibility, runtime experiment changes, existing saved visibility preferences, insufficient-scope labels, and cancellation recovery through Starting back to AuthRequired with a retry.
- ESLint and commit hygiene pass.
- Ten screenshot fixtures rendered successfully: five states in dark and light themes, using the real chat and dropdown components with fixture data.
- Full client type-check remains blocked by unrelated SDK/type errors in this checkout. Before rebasing, comparison with unmodified HEAD showed 51 existing errors and zero introduced errors; the post-rebase check reports no diagnostics in the changed files.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch an Agents Window chat while the MCP-auth pill experiment is disabled (default).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionChatInputToolbar constructs SessionMcpServers, but the derived sections return immediately after reading the false configuration value; MCP state acquisition is off the rendering critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live chat toolbars; each retains only a configuration/event observer while disabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One lightweight configuration observer per live chat toolbar; configuration events are processed synchronously, and strict equality suppresses unchanged boolean values.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No MCP session-state subscription is created while disabled. Configuration changes are observed so enabling takes effect without reload.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the enabled guard precedes both the session read and getMcpServers call, and observableFromEvent suppresses unchanged boolean values.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of split chat views varies, but disabled-state work is constant and does not scan MCP/customization state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: default-off construction does not cross an expensive boundary or perform collection work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, switch, or receive MCP/customization state updates in a chat with the experiment enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pill derives sections synchronously before the toolbar can present current auth-required servers. On a cold session read, getMcpServers resolves the target and establishes the session-state subscription; warm updates read the already-materialized snapshot, filter presentable servers, and update the pill presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a live agent-host Session state subscription through connection.getSubscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cached subscription per distinct session resource, shared across all split chat views and repeated reads for that session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the session chat toolbar alone did not request MCP state. Other customization consumers could already create the same cached subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold acquisition is initiated by the first enabled pill read, but the synchronous read can render an empty result until the asynchronous snapshot event arrives; it does not block toolbar rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct opened sessions control cold subscription count; live split chat views and customization/MCP server count control warm synchronous work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold subscription creation is coalesced by WorkbenchAgentHostCustomizationService's per-session DisposableResourceMap, so split views share one subscription. State events are handled serially on the UI thread; each live toolbar recomputes its own O(customizations + MCP servers) presentation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold reads create one service-level subscription per session; warm reads reuse it. The subscription is disposed when the chat service disposes that session, on provisional rebinding, or with the service. Derived sections are not structurally memoized, so broad customization events allocate fresh arrays, but downstream presentation checks avoid DOM updates when labels/icons/ARIA are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the subscription, cache sharing, and O(view count × customization count) synchronous recomputation; lower magnitude concern because no per-event boundary fan-out or unconditional DOM rebuild occurs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Customization counts and event frequency are typically small; broad events can make multiple live split views recompute, but the traced work is bounded, in-memory after the cold subscription, and lacks evidence of user-visible latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance regression. The single cached, non-blocking subscription is necessary for live auth status, and repeated in-memory work is bounded with presentation-level update suppression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click a single-server sign-in pill or choose one server from the multi-server dropdown.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user action awaits authenticateMcpServer, which starts the selected server and runs interactive MCP authentication; this is intentionally on the action's completion path, not chat startup/rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionMcpServerStartRequested to the owning agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch for the selected server per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing authentication service and server-management UI already used this operation; the diff adds a new explicit UI entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before interactive authentication can complete; user initiated and limited to the selected server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform interactive OAuth/authentication for the selected MCP endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One flow for the selected server per click, subject to the existing authentication service's token/cache behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existing authentication path was reachable from MCP server management; this diff routes the pill action to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action awaits the authentication result, as required for sign-in; it does not block unrelated chat rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User clicks, not total number of listed servers; multiple servers are displayed in a dropdown rather than authenticated eagerly.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One authentication attempt per explicit click. The new code does not loop over servers or launch concurrent attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Server lookup uses the current materialized session snapshot. Authentication/token caching and cancellation behavior remain owned by the existing resolver; the diff adds no new cache or retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the closure captures one resource/server id and calls the existing authentication method once.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote authentication duration depends on provider and user interaction, but cardinality is exactly one selected server per explicit action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the expensive work is explicit, single-target, and semantically required.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and relevant service/rendering call paths. The feature is default-off, enabled state uses one cached non-blocking session subscription, warm updates perform bounded in-memory scans with downstream presentation suppression, and authentication remains one user-initiated existing boundary call per selected server. No valid performance finding or regression-fix record was identified.
